+title: Frontmatter split on the bare substring "---" corrupts any card whose comment contains it
+---
+`parse_frontmatter_body` splits the entity file on the **substring** `-` `-` `-`, not on a line-anchored delimiter.
+
+`crates/swissarmyhammer-entity/src/io.rs:345`:
+
+```rust
+// Split on --- delimiters: ["", frontmatter, body]
+let parts: Vec<&str> = content.splitn(3, "---").collect();
+```
+
+A triple-dash anywhere inside the frontmatter block ends the frontmatter early. Every key after that point falls into the body and is lost from the entity.
+
+## How it was found
+
+Hit live on 2026-07-31 while working ^tnr56gg. The implementer wrote a progress comment that quoted a triple-dash inside backticks (it was describing this very parser). The comment lives in the frontmatter, so the split fired inside it. Result on `get task`:
+
+- `title` came back `""`
+- `position.column` came back `""` — the card fell off its column
+- `description` came back as the tail of the comment plus the leaked `position_column` / `position_ordinal` / `title` lines
+
+The on-disk bytes were still intact; only the read was wrong. That is the dangerous part — the next read-modify-write would have persisted the loss. Repaired by hand by rewording the comment.
+
+## Blast radius
+
+Frontmatter carries `comments[].text`, and comment text is free-form agent and human prose. A triple dash is ordinary in that prose: a markdown horizontal rule, a YAML document marker, a diff hunk, a Rust doc separator, an ASCII table rule. Every one of those silently destroys the card on the next write.
+
+Descriptions are safe — `splitn(3, ..)` leaves everything after the second delimiter in the body, so a triple dash in the body stays in the body. The exposure is frontmatter-only.
+
+## Required change
+
+Anchor the delimiter to a line: the opening delimiter is a line that is exactly three hyphens at the start of the file, and the frontmatter ends at the next line that is exactly three hyphens. A triple dash inside a YAML block scalar (indented, so not a bare delimiter line) must not terminate the frontmatter.
+
+Check `format_frontmatter_body` on the write side for the mirror-image assumption.
+
+## Acceptance
+
+- A task whose comment text contains a bare triple dash on its own line inside a block scalar round-trips with `title`, `position_column`, and every other frontmatter key intact. Prove it RED first with the real ^tnr56gg comment text as the fixture.
+- A task whose comment contains an indented triple dash round-trips.
+- The existing `parse_frontmatter_body_round_trip` test keeps passing.
+- A malformed file with no closing delimiter still returns `EntityError::InvalidFrontmatter` rather than silently treating the whole file as frontmatter. #bug #kanban
\ No newline at end of file
